answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated escrowed trades with counterparties that stake their own funds and suffer a loss when a trade is disputed and evidence shows fraud. The ledger caps how much influence fresh accounts gain, so splitting capital across many identities does not multiply trust; each new account must fund separate stakes and build history. A sybil attacker therefore ties up more capital and risks losing it for every identity, whether naming one yarrow, sonnet, or walnut.
